name: quality_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the 3-minute EMA (EMA-36) diverges above the 10-minute EMA (EMA-120) AND the gap is actively widening over the prior 30 seconds, this signals large institutional TWAP/VWAP programs are accumulating at multiple timescales simultaneously — not just a brief noise spike but a sustained directional program. The EMA gap acceleration distinguishes a live institutional order from a decaying imbalance: if each successive 5-second bar is adding to the gap, the program has not finished. A 5-minute ROC above 15 bps confirms the move has macro follow-through across the prior 60 bars. The VWAP position filter ensures the trade aligns with the session's dominant order flow direction, filtering entries where spot has already overshot.

indicators.name: ema_fast_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute EMA — trade trigger for fast directional momentum. Original used EMA(9) on 1-min bars = 9-min horizon. We compress to 3-min (36 × 5s) because at 5-second resolution we trade the fast momentum burst (30-90s hold), not the full 20-60 minute institutional program. The 3-min EMA captures the acceleration leg already in progress.

indicators.name: ema_slow_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute EMA — context filter for the dominant intraday trend. Original used EMA(21) on 1-min bars = 21-min horizon. We use 10-min (120 × 5s) as the 'slow' baseline: institutional TWAP programs running for 10+ minutes create the floor/ceiling we're trading the continuation of. Shorter than original because our session entry start is 09:30 (15 min after open) and we need the slow EMA to have enough history.

indicators.name: ema_gap_accel_6bar
indicators.formula: ema_gap[i] > ema_gap[i-6] (bullish) | ema_gap[i] < ema_gap[i-6] (bearish), where ema_gap = ema_fast - ema_slow
indicators.purpose: 6-bar (30 seconds) EMA gap acceleration — the key differentiator from plain crossover strategies. Original required 'EMA(9)-EMA(21) widening vs 5 bars ago on 1-min bars = 5 minutes ago'. At 5s, 6 bars = 30 seconds. If the gap is still widening 30 seconds in, the institutional order is still active. This is the quality-analog: momentum that is sustained over 30 seconds is more likely to continue than a one-bar spike.

indicators.name: roc_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute rate of change — confirms the move has macro follow-through. Original used ROC(30) on 1-min bars = 30-min horizon. We compress to 5-min (60 × 5s) rather than 12x scaling (360 bars = 30-min) because the trade trigger lookback scales with hold time, not the original's hold time. For a 30-90s trade, a 5-min ROC is the relevant 'medium-term' context — too much further back and you're measuring stale momentum.

indicators.name: vwap_session
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume), reset at session open per day_id
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP — filters direction relative to dominant order flow. No scaling needed: cumulative from session open regardless of bar size. Close > VWAP = bullish session bias; close < VWAP = bearish. Aligns with institutional VWAP benchmark behavior.

conditions: ema_gap widening over prior 30 seconds (6 bars): ema_gap[i] > ema_gap[i-6]
close > vwap_session (price above session VWAP — bullish bias)
VIX < 25 (high-volatility filter: above 25, gap accelerations fail more frequently)
buy_ce.confirmation: EMA gap must be positive (ema_gap > ema_gap_min, default 0.5 pts) to exclude near-zero crossovers

conditions: ema_gap widening bearishly over prior 30 seconds: ema_gap[i] < ema_gap[i-6]
close < vwap_session (price below session VWAP — bearish bias)
buy_pe.confirmation: EMA gap must be sufficiently negative (ema_gap < -ema_gap_min) to exclude noise crossovers

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts = ~6 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. If EMA acceleration thesis is correct, NIFTY should not retrace 6 spot points within 30-90 seconds of entry. The 6 spot-point threshold is approximately the typical NIFTY noise range in a 30-second window (2-5 option pts at 30s per calibration table); a 3-pt option stop sits just outside this noise, exiting when the thesis clearly breaks.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts = ~10 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. At 30-90 second holds, NIFTY acceleration moves extend 8-15 spot points (3-7 option pts for 1-min, per calibration table). 5 option pts captures the lower half of the typical 1-min extension range, giving 1:1.67 R:R with the 3-pt stop — viable at 55%+ directional accuracy.

filters.vix_filter: VIX < 25; above 25, EMA gap signals produce more false starts due to choppy institutional behavior
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; first 15 minutes excluded to allow EMA-120 warmup (120 bars = 10 min) and opening range noise to settle
filters.volume_filter: None explicit — NIFTY index volume is reliable at 5s resolution
filters.trend_filter: EMA gap direction is itself the trend filter; no additional trend filter needed
filters.spread_filter: None — limit order execution model, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Moderate — EMA-based signals are well-known but the gap acceleration confirmation reduces crowding; however, competing algos watching the same EMA crossover means signal edge can erode if too many participants enter on the same bar

adaptation_notes: The original strategy's 'quality filter' (ROE > 15%, D/E < 1.0, 4 consecutive positive quarters) is equity-specific and cannot be applied to a single index. The adaptation preserves the strategy's core signal structure — EMA crossover WITH widening gap confirmation + medium-term momentum + VWAP position — while discarding the stock-selection layer. The NIFTY index is inherently a quality-weighted instrument (cap-weighted, dominated by large-cap institutional favorites), so the quality thesis is embedded in the instrument itself. The key adaptation is: (1) EMA periods compressed from 9-min/21-min to 3-min/10-min to match 30-90s hold time instead of 20-60 min; (2) ROC compressed from 30-min to 5-min for same reason; (3) Gap acceleration window compressed from 5-min to 30-seconds (6 bars). The original's ATR-based stop converted to 3 option points (calibrated to typical NIFTY 30-90s move range).
weaknesses: EMA crossover signals at 5-second resolution can produce rapid whipsaws during NIFTY's 09:15-09:30 opening volatility — mitigated by 09:30 session start filter
Gap acceleration confirmation (30-second window) may be too fast during high-VIX days when institutional programs pause/restart frequently

No volume confirmation — NIFTY index volume is pre-aggregated at 5s and less informative than equity tick volume; quality of volume signal is weaker than the original equity strategy's SMA(volume, 15) filter
